name: Carlton
description: Melbourne's historic Italian quarter, home to the University of Melbourne and the famous Lygon Street restaurant strip. A walkable inner-city neighbourhood with strong community connections and easy CBD access.
vibe: Academic, multicultural, cafe culture, historic charm
transport: Tram routes 1, 6, 8 along Swanston Street and Nicholson Street. Short walk or bike ride to CBD. Near Melbourne Central and Parliament stations.
demographics: Large international student population alongside established Italian-Australian and East African communities. Mix of long-term residents and students.

name: Brunswick
description: A vibrant, multicultural inner-north suburb known for its eclectic food scene along Sydney Road, independent shops, and thriving arts community. Popular with young professionals and creatives.
vibe: Artsy, progressive, multicultural food hub, independent spirit
transport: Route 19 tram along Sydney Road. Jewell, Brunswick, and Anstey stations on the Upfield train line. Well-connected cycling paths.
demographics: Historically Turkish, Lebanese, and Greek communities. Now highly diverse with young professionals, families, and growing East African and South Asian populations.

name: Footscray
description: One of Melbourne's most culturally diverse suburbs, featuring vibrant Vietnamese, African, and Indian communities. An affordable inner-west neighbourhood with an energetic food and arts scene and a strong community spirit.
vibe: Gritty, diverse, authentic, rapidly evolving, community-driven
transport: Footscray station is a major hub on multiple train lines (Werribee, Williamstown, Sunbury). Multiple bus routes. Short train ride to CBD.
demographics: Extremely diverse with established Vietnamese, Ethiopian, Eritrean, Somali, and Indian communities. Growing number of young professionals alongside long-standing migrant families.

name: Fitzroy
description: Melbourne's bohemian heart and the birthplace of the city's street art and live music culture. While increasingly gentrified, it retains a strong community spirit with significant Aboriginal community presence and progressive social services.
vibe: Bohemian, artistic, progressive, street art, live music
transport: Tram routes 11, 86, and 96 along Brunswick Street, Smith Street, and Nicholson Street. Close to CBD by tram or bike.
communityGroups: The Fitzroy Town Hall community programs
demographics: Historic Aboriginal community presence alongside established public housing residents, creative workers, and young professionals. Significant gentrification over the past two decades.

name: Richmond
description: An inner-city suburb famous for its Vietnamese precinct on Victoria Street, with close proximity to the MCG and Melbourne's sporting precinct. Diverse dining, easy CBD access, and a mix of residential styles from public housing to renovated terraces.
transport: Richmond, East Richmond, and Burnley train stations. Tram routes 70, 78, and 109. Walking distance to CBD and MCG.
demographics: Established Vietnamese community on Victoria Street, alongside Greek and Chinese communities. Large public housing estates in the north. Mix of long-term residents and young professionals.

name: CBD/Melbourne Central
description: The city centre and heart of Melbourne, home to the Free Tram Zone, Chinatown, and major cultural institutions. A hub for international students, workers, and visitors with extensive services, shopping, and dining options.
transport: Free Tram Zone covers the entire CBD. Flinders Street, Melbourne Central, Southern Cross, and Flagstaff stations. All metropolitan train lines converge here.
demographics: Extremely international with large Chinese, Indian, South-East Asian, and Korean student and resident populations. Melbourne's Chinatown is the longest continuous Chinese settlement in the Western world.

name: St Kilda
description: Melbourne's iconic beachside suburb with a colourful character, popular with backpackers, artists, and young professionals. Known for its foreshore, Luna Park, and Sunday markets. A lively community with strong support services.
vibe: Beachside, eclectic, lively nightlife, artistic, community markets
transport: Tram routes 3, 16, and 96 from the CBD (about 20-25 minutes). Limited direct train access; nearest station is Balaclava on the Sandringham line.
communityGroups: Sacred Heart Mission (community meals and support)
demographics: Mix of backpackers, international visitors, long-term residents, and people accessing community support services. Historically bohemian with an increasingly young professional population.

name: Dandenong
description: One of Australia's most culturally diverse suburbs, located in Melbourne's south-east. Home to thriving Afghan, Indian, and Sri Lankan communities with an excellent multicultural food scene and affordable housing.
transport: Dandenong station on the Pakenham and Cranbourne train lines (about 40 minutes from CBD). Major bus interchange. Located on the Princes Highway.
communityGroups: Greater Dandenong City Council multicultural programs
demographics: Born-overseas residents from over 150 countries. Large Afghan, Indian, Sri Lankan, Chinese, and Pacific Islander communities. One of Australia's most diverse local government areas.

name: Clayton
description: A south-eastern suburb anchored by Monash University's main campus. Strong South Asian and Chinese community presence with excellent Asian dining options along Clayton Road and Centre Road.
vibe: University town, suburban, multicultural food scene, student-friendly
transport: Clayton station on the Cranbourne and Pakenham train lines (about 30 minutes from CBD). Multiple bus routes including connections to Monash University.
demographics: Large Chinese, Indian, Sri Lankan, and Malaysian communities. Significant international student population from Monash University alongside established migrant families.

name: Sunshine
description: A major hub in Melbourne's western suburbs with a diverse population, affordable housing, and improving transport connections. Growing rapidly with new developments while maintaining its multicultural community character.
vibe: Diverse, affordable, community-oriented, developing, western suburbs hub
transport: Sunshine station is a major rail hub on the Sunbury, Bendigo, and Ballarat lines (about 20 minutes from CBD). Multiple bus routes. Planned Melbourne Airport Rail Link will run through Sunshine.
demographics: Established Vietnamese, Indian, Filipino, and South Sudanese communities. One of Melbourne's most diverse areas with residents from over 150 countries. Growing young professional population.

name: Kensington
description: A quiet inner-west suburb with tree-lined streets, close to the CBD and Flemington Racecourse. Small but tight-knit community with a mix of young families and long-term residents. Easy access to the city via train.
vibe: Quiet, family-friendly, village feel, close to everything
transport: Kensington station on the Craigieburn/Sunbury line. Tram 57 runs along Racecourse Road. Short train ride to Southern Cross and the CBD. Good cycling paths along the Moonee Ponds Creek trail.
communityGroups: Flemington and Kensington Community Legal Centre
demographics: Mix of young families, professionals, and established residents. Growing African and Middle Eastern communities. Close proximity to Flemington's large Horn of Africa community.
